title: Secure Agentic Coding through Counterexample-Grounded Feedback
abstract: arXiv:2610.25916v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As coding models and agent harnesses become more capable, reliable security verification is becoming a central bottleneck. Improving secure code generation requires a signal whose reported progress remains aligned with actual program behavior under optimization; otherwise, an optimizer can improve the signal's verdict without removing the underlying vulnerability. Existing model-based approaches require models to either infer program behavior from source code or specify correct outcomes for adversarial tests, placing substantial reasoning demands on the security signal. We introduce \falcon{}, a counterexample-grounded verification framework that separates attack exploration from behavioral verification and connects them through execution traces of the program under test. In test-time repair, \falcon{} yields substantially stronger held-out functional-security gains than alternative security signals across secure code generatio

translated_title: 通过反例验证反馈实现安全的智能体编程
translated_abstract: 随着编程模型和智能体框架的能力不断提升，可靠的安全验证正成为核心瓶颈。改进安全代码生成需要一个信号，其报告的进展在优化过程中能与实际程序行为保持一致；否则，优化器可能在不移除底层漏洞的情况下提高该信号的判定结果。现有的基于模型的方法要求模型要么从源代码推断程序行为，要么为对抗性测试指定正确结果，这对安全信号提出了很高的推理要求。我们提出了FALCON，一个以反例为依据的验证框架，它将攻击探索与行为验证分离开来，并通过被测程序的执行轨迹将二者连接起来。在测试时修复任务中，FALCON在安全代码生成的各类基准上相比其他安全信号取得了显著更强的留出集功能-安全综合性能提升。
tldr: 提出了FALCON验证框架，通过将攻击探索与行为验证分离并以程序执行轨迹相连接，利用反例为安全信号提供可靠依据，从而在安全代码生成和测试时修复任务中显著提升功能性-安全性的综合表现。
en_tdlr: Introduces FALCON, a counterexample-grounded verification framework that separates attack exploration from behavioral verification via program execution traces, yielding substantially stronger functional-security gains in secure code generation and test-time repair.
